access.edition_or_version: Lippincott's Monthly Magazine (July 1890, shorter text); expanded book edition April 1891 with author's preface; public-domain text

mechanics.premise: A painter's portrait ages and corrupts in its subject's place while the sitter keeps his appearance, as he is talked out of conventional restraint into a life of sensation.
mechanics.point_of_view: Third-person limited, following Dorian, with narrative diction that increasingly borrows Lord Henry's epigrammatic manner — the cynical voice literally colonizes the narration.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Epigram and paradox as philosophical weapon; aestheticized description; the portrait as double; chapters in which feeling is deflated into theory by a single clever sentence.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Vanity awakened -> seduction by doctrine -> corrosion -> horror at evidence -> collapse, with each moral hesitation dissolved by a well-made sally.
mechanics.dialogue: Lord Henry's drawing-room epigrams do the philosophical work: each one re-describes a conventional virtue (duty, innocence, self-sacrifice) as folly or fraud before Dorian can hold it.
mechanics.conventions: Fin-de-siecle aestheticism and the Gothic double; the preface frames art's relation to morality, while the novel dramatizes what an all-deflating wit licenses.
tone_mechanisms: epigrammatic deflation of stated Victorian virtue
cynical voice as seductive influence on a character
mechanics.critical_reception: 1890 magazine version published amid obscenity concern; 1891 expanded edition with preface; now regarded as a classic of Gothic and English literature.
mechanics.verification_note: Existence, dates (Lippincott's July 1890; expanded April 1891), and genre status confirmed via Wikipedia API extract (The Picture of Dorian Gray) on 2026-09-24; edition and contextual cross-reference via the silo's Oxford Companion record. Analysis is partial: the tone-relevant method (epigrammatic deflation concentrated in Lord Henry) is described from documented accounts, not from a passage-level reading this session; no text reproduced.
